parts.note: capital is an old-fashioned British exclamation meaning excellent
to win something is to gain it, so wins gives gains

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their excellent run of victories has brought in a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital gains are the profits made when an asset is sold for more than it cost.

clue.text: English coin of yesteryear, editor learned

parts.note: the ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe in earlier centuries

explanation.surface: An English antique coin and a newspaper editor who knows a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone well schooled, having acquired much knowledge through study.

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece for working sits beneath the piece for Irish

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on

explanation.surface: Something is in use beneath an Irish golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a type of golf club with a metal head, used for mid-range shots.

clue.text: Small lock of hair causing anxiety

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A tiny strand of hair is making someone worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental strain or worry, so it is a synonym for anxiety.

parts.note: fair and right both mean just or proper
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: A funfair was called off without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as a funfair in the surface, but here it is the adjective meaning just.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something right off means doing it at once, without delay.

indicators.note: in a down clue over signals the word for objections is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: People complain about a discarded cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short remaining stump of a cigarette after smoking.

indicators.note: avoiding says the letter for large is kept out of the word for run

parts.note: a run in tights or stockings is called a ladder in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone flees, steering clear of a big snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb but is a noun: a ladder is the British word for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, also called the viper.

parts.note: a twin is one of a pair, and twin can mean paired

indicators.note: returned says the word for however is read backwards

parts.note: but and however both introduce a contrast

explanation.surface: Two people send back a washing machine after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is an older style of washing machine with separate tubs for washing and spinning.

clue.text: Courage shown by batsman at the start, one removing cap?

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
in cricket the opener is a batsman who begins the innings

explanation.surface: A cricketer opening the innings shows nerve and perhaps takes off his cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The cap is a bottle top, not a cricket cap; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle-opener is a tool that prises the metal cap off a bottle.

clue.text: Enrage church hemmed in by pubs close to centre

indicators.note: hemmed in by says the church letters sit inside the word for pubs

parts.note: inns are pubs
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word centre

explanation.surface: A church surrounded by central pubs makes people furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them very angry, a synonym of enrage.

clue.text: Usual practice of a bishop wearing belt

indicators.note: wearing says the word for belt goes around the other pieces like clothing

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop habitually wears a belt with his robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' looks like a garment the bishop wears, but it is the verb meaning strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a regular custom or settled tendency, something done routinely.

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion
as to means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A fresh idea about what to serve before the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables served before a meal.

clue.text: Under pressure, European married, penniless, in Welsh town

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
broke is slang for having no money

explanation.surface: A stressed European newlywed is out of money while living in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under pressure' reads as stressed, but 'Under' only links: P sits at the top of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is a historic town in south-west Wales, known for its castle.

clue.text: Drink brought back for close friend

indicators.note: brought back says the word for drink is read backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone fetched a drink for their mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is an informal word for a friend or mate.

indicators.note: mysteriously suggests the letters of poisoned are rearranged in an unexplained way

explanation.surface: A deity of Greek myth was poisoned in strange circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon was the Olympian ruler of the sea in Greek mythology.

parts.note: a shot at something is a go or attempt
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A hero was shot and killed.
explanation.definitionFit: A god can be a revered figure, so an idol is one, worshipped or adored.

clue.text: Aims often set out in this

definitions.text: Aims often set out in this

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters of aims often are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A document in which goals are commonly listed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a party's goals are set out in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published declaration of a party's policies and intentions.

indicators.note: no says the letter for litres is dropped from the word for annoyed

parts.note: needled means irritated or annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated that no litres were demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary or wanted.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word for judge is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: Collect a well-liked judge who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' is the sense of conclude, not collect.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather can mean to deduce or conclude, the same as to infer.

definitions.meaning: a standard is a banner or ensign carried on a pole
to decline is to weaken or tire, as energy does

explanation.surface: Levels are falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a banner, and to flag is to tire or lose strength.

parts.note: a motive is the cause or reason behind an action

explanation.surface: An Eastern movement stirs up passionate emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive describes something that stirs strong emotion, such as a heated topic.

clue.text: Said to come from Aurora Leigh

indicators.note: to come from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quotation is attributed to Aurora Leigh, the heroine of Elizabeth Barrett Browning's verse novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, so it is a synonym of said as an adjective.

clue.text: Author Muriel has the French fizz

parts.note: Muriel Spark was the Scottish novelist who wrote The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The novelist Muriel Spark has some French champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkle describes the bubbling effervescence of a drink like champagne.

parts.note: a rose is a familiar garden flower

explanation.surface: A plant bloomed suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose means came into being or got up, the past tense of arise.
